To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the dynamics of brain networks in infants with severe early epileptic encehpalopathies can be distinguished from the dynamics of networks in healthy infants, and that this is reflected in measures that quantify the smoothness of transitions between network patterns.

(i) we introduce a set of novel quantitative network measures to characterise EEG dynamics in healthy infants and patients with severe epilepsy; (ii) these measures are sensitive to the presence of epilepsy and can distinguish healthy infants and patients; (iii) these measures may be useful in the future for the diagnosis of epilepsy.
the early epilepsies can be distinguished from controls by a set of quantitative measures of network dynamics.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the dynamics of brain activity in the healthy and diseased brain.
the development of novel quantitative measures of network-level EEG dynamics, and their application to the analysis of spontaneous activity in infants with early epileptic encephaopathies.
the dynamics of brain networks, and how they change during development and in disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the EEGs of the early infantile epilepsies are characterised by a more dynamic and more variable brain network state switching than in the healthy controls.
the epileptic brain is characterised by a different dynamic network state switching than the healthy brain.
the epileptiform EEGs of the infants with EIEEs show more frequent and larger changes in correlation patterns than the EEGs of the controls.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed a new method for quantitative network analysis of spontaneous brain activity, and applied this method to a cohort of infants with epilepsy and controls, showing that the method is able to distinguish between groups.
the epileptic encephapathy is associated with changes in network dynamics.
the EEG of patients with early epileptic encehlopathies is characterised by a reduced smoothness of network dynamics.
The main takeaway from our work is that
quantitative measures derived from network dynamics may help to distinguish different groups of patients with early epileptic encepalopathies from controls.

the dynamics of the developing brain is not only reflected in the time evolution of the power of the different frequency bands, but also in the temporal evolution of the correlation structure across the brain.
